A.first_sentence: A passenger slams into your cabin door with one green hand caught in the gap, and the ship keeps sailing away from shore.
A.promise: Zombie Outbreak: 30 Days Trapped on a Cruise Ship
A.payoff: For the first time in thirty days, the floor beneath you does not move.
A.comparison: Compared immediate problems/constraints against actual saved bunker, day1-outbreak and 30th-floor openings. No view/retention prediction.

loop_ledger: Intact starboard boat is seen before the missing handle is discovered and recovered.
Ellis causes pantry breach; later waits quietly at hatch and helps gate/boat crossing.
Storm closes cabin refuge and forces workshop/boat plan; launch ends the drifting-ship threat.

opens.quote: You force the door shut and hold it until the latch catches. Across the ship, a lifeboat still hangs on the starboard side. But the corridor between you and it is filling with infected passengers. You have to reach that boat before this ship carries you beyond any chance of getting ashore.

closes.quote: Before sunset, the lifeboat scrapes sand. Ellis climbs out and holds the bow line while you and Mara step ashore. He can still walk on his sore knee. You carry the supplies clear of the water and help pull the boat higher.

opens.quote: A note on the lifeboat board identifies the covered boat you saw earlier as starboard boat three. Its release handle was taken to the lower workshop for repair before departure. The other starboard boats were damaged during boarding. This one is intact because nobody could launch it.

closes.quote: Mara fits the recovered handle into its marked socket. Ellis holds the access gate while you brace it with a fallen lounge chair. By the time the infected return, all three of you are behind the barrier.

opens.quote: Ellis is beyond it, calling his sister's name in a harsh whisper that carries too far. An infected crewman turns from the dish station. Then another rises behind the counter. Ellis backs toward you, empty handed, and for a second you think he has found her.

closes.quote: Ellis does not call out. He throws the empty cloth bag toward the far end of the promenade. It flutters, lands, and slides. The infected follow the motion just long enough for Mara to open the lifeboat access gate.

chronological_payoffs: Days1-5: cabins, Mara, pantry, Ellis and lifeboat observation.
Day6: Ellis opens galley; pantry lost, second laundry barrier installed.
Days7-16: recovered keys, limited crew supplies, bridge and missing release handle; storm.
Days18-20: cabins abandoned; failed workshop route and flashlight lost.
Days21-26: inspect alternate route, locker/chute/workshop, handle recovered, sore knee, promenade access.
Days27-29: rough water and snagged lowering line delay launch; final supplies.
Day30: three launch together, land and inspect boathouse.
